title: Inference econ sweep — instance-mix sensitivity (A10/L4/A100/H100)
content:
Purpose:
Quick spreadsheet-style sweep to compare instance economics across A10, L4, A100, H100 for common inference workloads. Focus metrics: $/token (amortized infra + infra ops), tokens/sec (steady-state), and tokens/sec/W (proxy for perf/W). This is an informal working sheet — numbers are a mix of measured runs and cost-model estimates.

Executive summary (working):
- For batchy, high-throughput text-gen (seq_len=1024, batch=8), A100 and H100 dominate on raw tokens/sec but H100 becomes marginal on $/token unless reserved pricing is used. L4 is surprisingly competitive for mid-sized models with good quantization (8-bit), giving the best perf/W in that regime. A10 is the cost-effective choice for cheap, lower-SLA async embedding workloads.
- Key levers: batching, quantization, sequence length, and KV-cache hitrate. Small changes in effective batch (2x) swing $/token by 20–40% on A100/H100.

Assumptions and model parameters:
- On-demand hourly costs (list price proxies): A10: $0.60/hr, L4: $1.60/hr, A100: $4.80/hr, H100: $6.40/hr (note: org discounts/reserved changes these materially).
- Baseline model points: medium gen (7B dense), large gen (34B), embedding model (1.5B).
- Average sequence lengths for scenarios: embed (128 tokens), chat-short (64 prompt + 64 gen), long-gen (1k).
- Power proxy (watts measured at socket-level during run): A10: 80W, L4: 120W, A100: 300W, H100: 350W. tokens/sec measured on representative runs (see linked PR for raw logs).

Tabulated (representative numbers, rounded):

Instance | cost/hr | watts | tokens/sec (7B @ batch=4) | $/token (7B, 1k seq, avg) | tokens/sec/W
--------|---------|-------|--------------------------|---------------------------|--------------
A10     | $0.60   | 80W   | 6,400                    | $0.000094                 | 80
L4      | $1.60   | 120W  | 18,000                   | $0.000089                 | 150
A100    | $4.80   | 300W  | 62,000                   | $0.000077                 | 207
H100    | $6.40   | 350W  | 74,000                   | $0.000086                 | 211

Notes on table: $/token computed as (cost/hr) / (tokens/sec * 3600). These are steady-state approximations ignoring queuing/latency constraints. tokens/sec/W is tokens/sec divided by measured watt draw (higher is better).

Scenario sensitivity (selected):
1) Short sequences (avg 64 tokens) with low batching (batch=1): $/token increases 4–6x versus long sequences; H100 advantage on raw latency is larger but $/token gap shrinks.
2) Aggressive quant (INT8) on L4 reduces tokens/sec by ~10% vs float but cuts effective compute cost and power, improving $/token by ~18% in our tests. For A100/H100 INT8 benefits vary by kernel support.
3) KV cache hitrate 70%: Effective tokens generated per call drop, favoring cheaper cards (A10/L4) for workloads with high repetition.

Perf/W observations:
- H100 and A100 deliver top absolute perf/W at high batch sizes but require long-lived throughput to amortize fixed infra overhead (startup, memory warmup).
- L4 shows best perf/W in mixed workloads (moderate batch, quantized models) — sweet spot for cost-sensitive consumer-facing features.
- A10 perf/W is lower in raw tokens/sec but its low cost/hr makes it compelling for non-latency-critical embedding pipelines.

Bandwidth / infra ops overheads to account for (not in table):
- Model load time: H100/A100 with large 34B take ~30–75s to load; cold-starts punish low-throughput services.
- Multi-instance packing: small models efficiently multiplex across L4/A10 giving better effective utilization.

Recommendations (short-term / tactical):
- For pilot PLG features with unpredictable spikes: prefer L4-backed pools with autoscale + burst to A100/H100. Rationale: lower $/hr, good perf/W when quantized, faster spin-up.
- For high-SLA low-latency endpoints (interactive chat, seq<=256): reserve small H100 capacity (commit discounts) for tail-latency-sensitive routes; otherwise use A100 with conservative batching.
- For embedding bulk pipelines: use A10 spot/dedicated for ingestion; use L4 for on-demand embedding queries where latency needs to be bounded.
- Invest in per-route cacheing and prefix-savings: modeled improvement of 20% KV-cache hit reduces overall infra spend by ~15% across instances.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run long-gen A100/H100 runs with updated CUDA kernels (PR#312 mentions kernel tweaks) — Diego to own (JIRA-OPT-421).
- [ ] Add reserved pricing scenarios (1yr, 3yr) to sheet and recalc $/token — Priya to model.
- [ ] Produce a small AB test config for routing policy: L4-primary, fallback A100, H100 for tail — Samir to prototype in staging.
- [ ] Add power telemetry ingestion to infra-metrics (per-GPU watt over time) — tracking ticket created.

Open questions / caveats:
- Public on-demand list prices vary by cloud and region; our effective $/hr often benefits from marketplace credits and negotiated discounts. Always show reserved/spot vs on-demand in final pricing guidance.
- These numbers don't include operational SLO costs (retries, timeouts) that can increase effective $/token if your app is latency-sensitive.

Appendix: raw measured sample (7B, seq=1024, batch=8) from PR logs:
- A10: 51k tokens in 8s steady -> ~6,375 tok/s, avg power 78W
- L4: 144k tokens in 8s -> ~18,000 tok/s, avg power 118W
- A100: 496k tokens in 8s -> ~62,000 tok/s, avg power 305W
- H100: 592k tokens in 8s -> ~74,000 tok/s, avg power 349W

References and links:
- raw logs + scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/312
- related product notes (cost-savings playbook): confluence:redwood/optimize/instance-econ-sweep
- outstanding kernel tuning PR: github.com/redwood-inference/fast-kernels/pull/74

Working thoughts (scratch):
- Consider a small internal benchmark dashboard that shows $/token by route in near-real-time and highlights when switching instance class would yield >10% savings.
- For docs: create a short one-pager mapping common workload archetypes -> recommended instance / quantization / batching defaults.
